item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,282 as two die in 24hrs
item.description:
Two children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours ending at 8:00am on Sunday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,282 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,177, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 105.
A total of 1,138 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, pushing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 238,840.
Meanwhile, 87 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 24,442.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 212,979 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 204,049 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: Shama: Rohingya crisis now a security concern for Bangladesh
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Sunday said the Rohingya crisis has become a security concern for Bangladesh, stressing the need to keep the issue high on the international agenda.
"We need to keep the Rohingya issue relevant on the international stage, and keeping it relevant remains a major challenge," she said while speaking as the chief guest at a dialogue.
Neeti Gobeshona Kendro organized the national policy dialogue titled "A Sustainable Approach to the Resolution of the Rohingya Crisis: Outline of a National Strategy and External Contribution" at the CIRDAP Auditorium.
The state minister said Bangladesh must press the international community to engage meaningfully with Myanmar to ensure that the necessary conditions are created inside the country for the safe and dignified return of the Rohingyas.
She also underscored the importance of building a national political consensus on addressing the crisis.
"We have always been vocal about the Rohingya crisis," Shama Obaed said emphasizing that repatriation must take place in a safe and dignified manner.
"We need to ensure minimum dignity for them," she said.
Bangladesh is currently hosting more than 1.3 million Rohingyas, with the number continuing to grow, putting increasing pressure on host communities and the country's economy as a whole.
The dialogue aimed to facilitate constructive engagement among policymakers, political leaders, diplomats, researchers, civil society representatives, human rights advocates, journalists and representatives of the Rohingya community on developing a sustainable and comprehensive approach to resolving the protracted crisis.
Particular emphasis was placed on formulating a national strategic framework, building political consensus, strengthening diplomatic engagement and exploring the roles of international and external stakeholders.
The discussion highlighted the importance of sustained policy dialogue, diplomatic engagement, political consensus and meaningful participation of the Rohingya community in finding a durable and dignified solution to one of the most protracted humanitarian and geopolitical challenges facing Bangladesh and the wider region.

item.title: Minister: Hasina is a convict, legal steps taken to bring her back
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Sunday said the government is following due legal procedures to bring ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh, describing her as a convicted criminal.
“To me, she is a criminal. She is a convict, sentenced by our tribunal. That is her identity to us. Legal procedures are underway to bring her back,” he said.
The minister made the remarks after inaugurating a workshop on "Integrity in Judicial Proceedings" organized by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) at a hotel in Dhaka.
“Whatever needs to be done legally concerning Sheikh Hasina, we are doing that through due process. You will see how we deal with it legally when we take any steps. There is no room for emotion here. The matter is that I will enforce the law. If we fail to enforce the law properly, then you can question us,” he said.
Asked whether the government would fight a legal battle in an Indian court to bring her back, the minister said it is a matter for the Indian government.
“We have sent a request to them under the extradition treaty. If they hand her over to us, we will bring her under the law through due process in the manner required,” he said.
When a journalist questioned the extradition treaty, saying Hasina was staying in India as a state guest rather than being held as a prisoner, Asaduzzaman said her status as described by Indian authorities did not change Bangladesh’s position.
“They may say whatever they want, but that is not enough. She was tried in an open court in my country. Since you are raising this question, first consider whether 1,400 people were killed during the July Revolution and whether 30,000 people were left disabled,” he said.
He also questioned whether the trial had any shortcomings, whether it was held behind closed doors and whether witnesses had been allowed to testify.
“We have sent the request that is required under due process to bring her back. That is what I am saying,” the minister added.

item.title: Kali Puja festivities set to begin across Bangladesh
item.description:
The Hindu communities across Bangladesh are celebrating Kali Puja, also known as Shyama Puja, on Sunday night with religious rituals, traditional festivities and prayers dedicated to Goddess Kali.
Temples and households are ready to welcome the auspicious occasion with special worship of Goddess Kali, illumination with earthen lamps and candles, devotional music and various religious rituals.
Kali Puja, popularly known as Deepabali or the festival of lights, is observed on the new moon night (Amavasya) of the Bengali month of Kartik. The festival is dedicated to Goddess Kali, regarded as the embodiment of divine power, strength, wisdom and the destruction of evil.
As part of the celebration, devotees will illuminate their homes, temples and crematoriums with earthen lamps (pradeep) and candles in remembrance of their ancestors.
In the capital, elaborate preparations have been made to celebrate the festival at Dhakeshwari National Temple, Ramkrishna Math and Mission, Siddheshwari Kali Mandir, Ramna Kali Mandir, Sri Sri Baradeshwari Kalimata Temple, Radha Gobinda Jeo Temple, Postogola Crematorium, Biharilal Jeo Temple in Sutrapur, Gautam Mandir, Ramseeta Mandir, Shibmandir in Shankharibazar, Tanti Bazar and Bangla Bazar.
According to the puja schedule, worship of Goddess Kali will begin at midnight at different temples, followed by the offering of anjali, “hom-joggo” and distribution of mahaprasad among the devotees.
According to Hindu mythology, Goddess Kali is a fierce manifestation of Goddess Durga, who emerged to fight the forces of evil. Legend has it that after a fierce battle with demonic forces, Kali became so consumed by her destructive rage that Lord Shiva had to lie beneath her feet to stop her.
Realizing that she had stepped on her consort, she stuck out her tongue in astonishment and brought her rampage to an end.
The key message of Kali Puja is the triumph of good over evil and the destruction of negative forces both in the external world and within human beings.
The largest celebrations in the capital traditionally take place in Shakhari Bazar and Tanti Bazarin Old Dhaka.
A festive atmosphere has already emerged in the two neighbourhoods, where makeshift pandals have been erected and temples decorated with colorful lights and ornamental designs.
Meanwhile, business activities related to the festival are gaining momentum in the old part of the capital, with devotees and families flocking to markets to purchase puja essentials, including candles, earthen lamps (pradeep) and other ritual items.

item.title: 33 BGB platoons deployed across Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj
item.description:
A total of 33 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj amid ongoing workers' unrest.
The deployment aims to maintain law and order, strengthen security in industrial zones and prevent further incidents, the BGB said in a statement issued on Sunday morning.
In Dhaka, BGB personnel are deployed in Savar, Ashulia and Mirpur.
In Narayanganj, they are overseeing security in Shibu Market, Jalkuri, the BSCIC Industrial Estate, Chashara, Kanchpur and Shimrail.
In Gazipur, the deployment covers Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Mouchak, Ambag, Kashimpur, Naojor, Bhogra Bypass, Gacha and Salna.
The BGB headquarters' monitoring cell is also monitoring field operations and live footage through technology-based systems, according to the statement.
Deployed personnel remain on high alert and are working in coordination with local administrations and police.
The BGB said deployment and surveillance operations would continue to maintain a safe and stable working environment in industrial areas, protect lives and property, and ensure public security.

item.title: Bus torched in Savar after three consecutive nights of fires in Dhamrai
item.description:
Two more buses were set on fire in separate incidents in Savar and Dhamrai early Sunday, taking the total number of buses torched in the two upazilas to four in four nights. No casualties were reported.
Jahangir Alam, senior station officer of Savar Fire Service, and Al-Amin Khan, station officer of Dhamrai Fire Station, confirmed the incidents on Sunday morning.
The fires broke out near the Savar Thana Bus Stand and in the Sharifbag area of Dhamrai, both along the Dhaka-Aricha Highway.
According to Savar Fire Service, it received a report of a fire involving a Savar Paribahan bus parked near the Savar Thana Bus Stand at 2:55am.
Two fire service units rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control by 3:10am.
Jahangir Alam said preliminary findings suggested that the bus had been set on fire. He estimated the damage at around Tk2 lakh.
Meanwhile, a D-Link Paribahan bus caught fire in front of Afaz Uddin College in Dhamrai’s Sharifbag area around 3:40am, according to the Dhamrai Fire Service.
Two units responded to the incident and extinguished the fire by 4:20am.
Al-Amin Khan said the bus was mainly used to transport employees of Snotex Garments to and from Nabinagar. It was parked when the fire broke out.
He said preliminary findings suggested that the bus had been deliberately set on fire.
The latest incident marks the third consecutive night of bus fires in Dhamrai. On Thursday night, November 5, a bus belonging to Pavel Paribahan, which was undergoing repairs, caught fire on Dhamrai Thana Road.
The following night, a Polli Seba Paribahan bus was set on fire in the Srirampur area along the Dhaka-Aricha Highway.
Dhamrai police station Officer-in-Charge Md Nazmul Huda Khan said three buses had been set on fire in the upazila over three consecutive nights.
He said police had advised bus owners after the previous incident to keep their vehicles in secure locations, under guard or close surveillance.
“Despite this, another bus left outside was set on fire. We are investigating whether these incidents are politically motivated, stem from personal disputes or are related to other factors,” he said.
The OC said the owner of one of the affected buses had filed a complaint with the police station. Police were treating the incidents seriously and working to establish the circumstances behind them.

item.title: Salam made convener as BNP reconstitutes Dhaka South city unit
item.description:
The BNP has reconstituted the convening committee of its Dhaka South city unit, appointing Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator Abdus Salam as convener and retaining Tanvir Ahmed Robin as member secretary.
The decision was announced in a press release signed by party’s Office Secretary Munir Hossain on Sunday.
Abdul Kadir Bhuiyan Jewel has been made senior joint convener, while ANM Saiful Islam has been appointed joint convener.
Before the reconstitution, Feni-1 MP Munshi Rafiqul Alam was the convener of the unit, while Robin served as its member secretary.
The latest move came after BNP formed a new convening committee for its Dhaka North unit on November 1.
Dhaka North City Corporation Administrator Safiqul Islam Khan was named convener of the North unit, while Dhaka-18 MP SM Jahangir Hossain was appointed its member secretary.

item.title: Brahmanbaria road, rail blockade lifted after 4hrs; protesters issue 72hrs ultimatum
item.description:
Residents lifted a four-hour blockade of roads and railway lines in Brahmanbaria on Sunday after receiving assurances from a local BNP leader over their demands to restore six villages to Basudeb Union and oppose the proposed formation of a new upazila.
The protesters called off the blockade around 11am after Sirajul Islam Siraj, general secretary of the district BNP and administrator of the district council, arrived at the scene and assured them that their demands would be addressed.
However, they warned that they would resume the blockade if their demands were not met within 72 hours.
The demonstration began at 7am in the Kodda area of Brahmanbaria Sadar Upazila, where residents blocked the Dhaka-Agartala highway and the Dhaka-Chittagong and Dhaka-Sylhet railway lines.
The blockade brought road traffic to a standstill in both directions and left at least seven intercity trains stranded at different stations, causing hardship for thousands of passengers.
Jahangir Alam Bhuiyan Nayan, president of Basudeb Union BNP, said several villages had recently been separated from Basudeb Union to form a new union named Barisal.
He alleged that residents of the affected villages, including Basudeb, Kodda, Chandi and Korabaria, were not consulted before the decision was made.
He also alleged that the new union was formed under the influence of district BNP leader Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan, whose father, Fazlur Rahman Bhuiyan, was appointed its administrator.
According to Jahangir, there are also plans to form a new upazila, also named Barishal, comprising several unions from Brahmanbaria Sadar and Bijoynagar upazilas.
The protesters are demanding that the separated villages be brought back under Basudeb Union and opposing the proposed upazila.
Dulal Mia, a resident of Chandi village, alleged that Kabir Ahmed Bhuiyan was driving the initiatives by using the influence of his brother, Abdur Rahman Sunny, who serves as assistant private secretary-2 to the prime minister.
No comments could be obtained from the individuals named in the allegations.
Sirajul Islam Siraj arrived at the protest site around 10:30am. Following his assurances, the protesters withdrew the blockade at around 11am, allowing road and rail services to resume.
The protesters reiterated that they would block both roads and railway lines again if their demands were not met within 72 hours.

item.title: More than orders: How trust helps Bangladesh’s RMG industry grow
item.description:
Bangladesh has grown into one of the world’s leading apparel manufacturing hubs. The RMG sector plays a key role in the country’s economy, creating millions of jobs and supporting thousands of local businesses.
In this environment, growth depends not only on production capacity or costs, but also on strong business relationships.
The experiences of suppliers working with LPP, today the eighth-largest sourcing partner in Bangladesh’s RMG sector, show how long-term cooperation can support business growth, investment, and workforce development.
It often starts with communication. In an industry where manufacturers face changing market conditions and daily challenges, open dialogue helps companies solve problems and plan for the future.
This is something Hasan Mahmud, managing director of Design Ace Limited, highlights as one of the key strengths of long-term cooperation: “This approach supports our operational stability and gives us greater confidence to invest in our capabilities and prepare for future growth.”
Strong communication also helps companies improve the way they work.
At Iris Design Limited, cooperation with a global retailer has encouraged better production planning, greater efficiency, and continuous skills development.
According to Marzia M Adhora, director of marketing & compliance at IRIS Group BD, mutual understanding and a willingness to solve challenges together have helped build lasting trust.
It also gives companies the confidence to invest. Bell Bottom is a good example. For the company, predictable business relationships with LPP created the foundation for long-term growth.
“A stable and reliable business partner gave us the confidence to invest in automation, ESG initiatives, and employee development. Those investments transformed our company from a team of three people into an organization employing 350 specialists, while our business expanded ninety-fold,” says Mohammad Saifuzzaman of Bell Bottom.
The value of such partnerships becomes even clearer during difficult periods, including supply chain disruptions or raw material price fluctuations.
“In an industry facing constant market volatility and operational challenges, constructive dialogue and cooperation create the stability businesses need to continue growing,” says Md Abul Kalam, managing director and CEO of Chaity Group.
These experiences show that the most valuable result of a business partnership is often not the order itself.
It is the confidence to invest, grow, and make long-term decisions. The stories of suppliers working with LPP demonstrate that trust can create the conditions for growth and business resilience.
In the global fashion industry, trust is increasingly proving to be capital just as important as money.

item.title: Prime Bank opens month-long ‘Entrepreneurship Development’ training in Sylhet
item.description:
Prime Bank PLC has recently inaugurated a month-long (100-hour) specialized training program titled ‘Entrepreneurship Development’ in Sylhet.
The program has been launched under the Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program (Sicip), implemented by the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance, with the overall supervision of Bangladesh Bank’s SME & Special Programs Department.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Nawshad Mustafa, director, Bangladesh Bank as chief guest, and Mohammad Wasim and Muhammad Ariful Islam, joint directors of Bangladesh Bank, were present as special guests.
The event was presided over by M Nazeem A Chowdhury, additional managing director, Prime Bank PLC.
Among others, the program was attended by Md Mohsinur Rahman, head of SME Banking, Prime Bank PLC; Shaikh Nur Alam, head of S Business & Refinance, and Md Humayun Kabir, regional head.
The primary objective of this training program is to enhance the business knowledge, management skills and industry- and market-oriented competencies of aspiring and existing Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) entrepreneurs.
The initiative aims to equip entrepreneurs with the necessary skills to manage and grow their businesses while promoting competitiveness and innovation across the country's industrial sector.
Prime Bank PLC believes that such skill-based training initiatives will play a significant role in nurturing new entrepreneurs, supporting the expansion of existing businesses and contributing to the sustainable economic development of the country.

item.title: BB eases LC conditions for 11 essential commodities ahead of Ramadan
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has relaxed conditions for opening Letters of Credit (LCs) for imports to ensure a smooth supply of essential commodities during the upcoming month of Ramadan.
From now on, commercial banks can determine the cash margin rate for opening LCs for designated goods based on their bank-customer relationships.
On Sunday (November 8), the Banking Regulations and Policy Department-1 of Bangladesh Bank issued a circular regarding this matter.
The directive has been sent to the managing directors and chief executive officers of all scheduled banks in the country.
The circular stated that the demand for essential daily items increases during Ramadan.
This initiative aims to facilitate imports, maintain a steady supply of goods in the market, and keep prices at a tolerable level during this period.
According to the guidelines, the cash margin for opening LCs for importing rice, wheat, onions, pulses, soybean and palm oil, sugar, chickpeas, yellow peas, spices, and dates can be settled on the basis of bank-customer relationships.
Additionally, the central bank advised commercial banks to prioritize importers when opening LCs to ensure an adequate supply of these commodities in the domestic market.
Bangladesh Bank noted that this directive was issued in the public interest using powers conferred under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991.
The order takes effect immediately and will remain in force until March 15, 2027.

item.title: Khasru: Found discrepancies in previous govt’s GDP calculations
item.description:
Massive discrepancies and inconsistencies have been identified in the calculation of the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) during the previous government's tenure.
The government announced that these anomalies were uncovered through a forensic audit, and the report will be made public shortly following expert review.
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and Minister of State for Planning Md. Jonayed Abdur Rahim Saki shared this information Sunday at a discussion meeting held at the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) auditorium in the capital, on the occasion of National Statistics Day.
At the same time, the government announced that full independence is being granted to the Bureau of Statistics (BBS) to restore the neutrality of data and public trust in statistics.
Speaking as the chief guest, Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury emphasized data transparency, stating that work cannot be carried out using questionable statistics as it is akin to deceiving oneself.
Pointing out that data is the government's most critical asset, he affirmed that BBS is being given complete independence.
Clarifying the review of past calculations, the minister stressed that the audit's purpose is not to target anyone personally. He noted that the forensic audit was conducted to delve into past irregularities, not to target individuals, adding that the more data is made open, the more errors and inconsistencies will surface, creating opportunities for correction.
The minister also mentioned that alongside addressing manpower shortages, the government is prioritizing digital infrastructure and the use of artificial intelligence in this tech era.
Adviser to the Ministry of Finance and Planning, Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, stated that during the previous government's tenure, statistics were weaponized to construct a specific political narrative.
Highlighting significant discrepancies in the list of social safety net beneficiaries alongside GDP data, the minister noted that many of those who genuinely deserved assistance were deprived.
Citing a concrete example of statistical discrepancy, the minister shared that the number of registered vessels in the country was previously shown as a mere 13,000, whereas a recent review revealed the actual number to be 267,000.
He announced that initiatives are underway to establish an integrated "Digital Register" system soon to eliminate such anomalies.
Speaking as a special guest, Minister of State for Planning Md. Jonayed Abdur Rahim Saki stated that without accurate data, it is impossible to understand where the country stands, where it intends to go, or where mistakes are occurring. Hence, initiatives have been launched to rebuild the public's lost faith in statistics.
The State Minister added that effective measures have already been taken to reduce government interference in data. As part of these measures, the BBS now directly releases all crucial economic metrics, including the Consumer Price Index (CPI), without requiring prior approval or signatures from any minister.
Chaired by Md Firoz Sarkar, secretary of the Statistics and Informatics Division, the event opened with welcome remarks by BBS Director General Md Shamimul Huq.
Additionally, Prime Minister's Political Adviser Zahir Uddin Swapan, Dhaka University Professor Syed Shahadat Hossain, and Director General of the Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies (BIDS) AK Enamul Haque also addressed the meeting.

item.title: HSBC commits $1bn for disaster preparedness in Bangladesh
item.description:
HSBC announced details of its disaster preparedness partnership in Bangladesh with Unicef, the British Red Cross and Save the Children, to support communities prepare for emergencies and enable HSBC funding to reach them faster when crises strike.
The activity forms part of HSBC’s Disaster Relief Partnership, backed by a commitment of $4.5 million over an initial 18-month pilot period, supporting projects in countries including Bangladesh, Vietnam, Kenya and the Philippines.
Launched globally on October 13, 2026, the partnership combines HSBC funding with the expertise and reach of three leading humanitarian organizations.
In Bangladesh, approximately $1 million has so far been allocated to support three specific disaster preparedness projects.
The projects will work to strengthen community preparedness and resilience, supporting early action ahead of predicted emergencies such as flooding or landslides, in helping to protect lives and livelihoods.
The “HSBC’s Disaster Relief Partnership - Launch in Bangladesh,” ceremony took place in Dhaka recently and was attended by Surendra Rosha, co-chief executive of Asia and Middle East, HSBC; Md Mahbub ur Rahman, chief executive officer of HSBC Bangladesh; Antonio Granco Garcia, chief of field service, Unicef Bangladesh; Mukesh Kumar Singh, country representative, the British Red Cross; Rahmat Ullah Bhuiyan, deputy country director, Save the Children; James Goldman, deputy high commissioner and development director to Bangladesh, British High Commission.
Surendra Rosha, co-chief executive of Asia and Middle East, HSBC said: “Long-term economic growth across our international markets depends directly on community resilience. By bringing together HSBC’s global reach and the frontline expertise of our humanitarian partners, we are helping vulnerable regions across Asia shift from simply reacting to crises to preparing for them before they happen.”
Commenting on the country launch, Md Mahbub ur Rahman, chief executive officer, HSBC Bangladesh said: “Economic resilience in Bangladesh starts with local preparedness. Through this collaboration with Unicef, the Red Cross, and Save the Children, we are putting resources where they matter most which is building long-term defenses so vulnerable communities can anticipate and withstand climate challenges.”
Antonio Franco García, chief field services of Unicef in Bangladesh said: “For children in Bangladesh, floods, cyclones and disease outbreaks can quickly become life-threatening emergencies. Investing in preparedness means acting before disaster strikes, not only responding afterwards. Through this partnership with HSBC, we will help vulnerable communities anticipate risks, act early and better protect children, building a safer and more resilient future for every child.”
Mukesh Singh, country representative, the British Red Cross, said: “Lasting change happens when communities have the power, resources, and support to act. Through HSBC’s partnership, the British Red Cross together with the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society can strengthen locally led preparedness, response, and climate action, enabling communities to better anticipate, adapt to, and recover from crises.”
ASM Rahmat Ullah, deputy country director, Save the Children said: “We acknowledge the support from HSBC which has strengthened Save the Children’s organizational systems for localized risk monitoring and anticipatory action while enabling timely, targeted support to the most vulnerable households ahead of an emergency, empowering communities to act early, build local resilience and minimize disaster impacts.”
This unique collaboration offers an important opportunity to learn and share best practices.
The partnership also aims to strengthen the collective ability of partners to provide HSBC support at pace, build resilience and support disaster mitigation efforts.

item.title: Stamford University VC calls for human-centered AI at 2026 IEEE conferences
item.description:
Stamford University Bangladesh Vice-Chancellor Sharif Nafe As-Saber highlighted the need for human-centered artificial intelligence (AI) and sustainable technology at the joint 2026 IEEE international conferences held in Cox’s Bazar from November 1-3.
The 12th IEEE International Conference on Sustainable Technologies for Engineering (i-COSTE 2026) and the 11th IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Computer Science and Data Engineering (CSDE 2026) brought together hundreds of researchers, engineers and data scientists from 35 countries.
Held in a hybrid format at the Best Western Heritage, the conferences were hosted by Bangladesh University of Business and Technology (BUBT) in technical collaboration with the IEEE Bangladesh Section and NPS Australia.
The joint event followed the theme “Sustainable Technology for Humanity and Global Impact.” While i-COSTE 2026 focused on green engineering, renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure, CSDE 2026 covered artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain, quantum computing and big data analytics.
As chief guest at the opening and closing ceremonies, As-Saber called for technology to serve practical purposes and improve human well-being rather than being pursued for its own sake. He advocated a human-centered AI framework that enhances human capabilities, protects dignity and prioritizes people's well-being over corporate automation.
He also stressed the need to develop Bangla-based AI tools and large language models to make the technology accessible to the wider population and help bridge the digital divide.
As-Saber urged Bangladesh to assess its readiness for AI and identify priority areas for its adoption, taking into account operational risks and environmental costs.
Highlighting the energy and water consumption associated with data centers, he proposed exploring underwater data storage solutions. He said Bangladesh's strategic location beside the Bay of Bengal could offer an opportunity to develop marine-cooled, energy-efficient data infrastructure.
He also called for AI education and training frameworks to be aligned with public policy, ethics, indigenous skills and local conditions.
BUBT Vice-Chancellor A B M Shawkat Ali chaired both the opening and closing ceremonies.
In his concluding remarks, As-Saber urged researchers, academics and businesses to develop cost-effective and sustainable technologies, including human-centered AI, for the benefit of the wider population.

item.title: Savar-Ashulia industrial activity normalises, 20 factories shut
item.description:
Industrial activity has largely returned to normal in Savar and Ashulia following several days of unrest over garment workers’ demands, including a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000 and an end to blacklisting.
Most factories resumed production on Sunday, although authorities declared holidays at 20 factories after workers at several facilities stopped working and remained inside their workplaces.
After the holiday announcements around 10:30am, workers from several factories took positions on the Abdullahpur-Baipail road. Police later persuaded them to leave the road. Speaking around noon, Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Ashulia Industrial Police-1, said workers were carrying out their duties peacefully at most factories in Savar and Ashulia.
However, workers at several factories had stopped working and remained inside, prompting the authorities to declare holidays at 20 factories. Workers at four factories were still refusing to work, he added.
He said some workers took to the streets, but police persuaded them to move away.
The Savar Upazila administration said 11 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), along with police personnel, had been deployed to maintain law and order, keep factories operational and ensure uninterrupted production.
Speaking around 12:45pm, Khairul Mamun, legal affairs secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre, said workers at several factories had returned to work.
However, authorities had declared holidays at some factories after workers stopped working and remained inside, while workers at a few others were still refusing to work.
Overall, the situation was satisfactory for the time being, he said, stressing that ensuring workers receive their wages by the 10th of the month should now be the top priority.
Savar Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Saiful Islam said the situation in the industrial areas of Savar was currently normal, with workers returning to their workplaces.
However, the period leading up to the 10th of the month would be crucial for wage payments, and the administration was closely monitoring the situation, he said.
Factory owners had been instructed to pay workers within the stipulated deadline.
The UNO added that 11 platoons of BGB, nine executive magistrates and members of various law enforcement agencies had been deployed to maintain normalcy in the area.

item.title: Cape Verde hero Vozinha struggles to cope with glare of fame
item.description:
After repelling eventual champions Spain and becoming an instant global celebrity, Vozinha was an unlikely hero of this year's World Cup. But four months on from his tournament exploits, Cape Verde's veteran goalkeeper is discovering that adapting to his new-found fame is not easy.
The 40-year-old, whose full name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, moved to Chile in July and now finds himself struggling to settle at new club Colo Colo.
At the World Cup, Vozinha helped Cape Verde hold Spain to a 0-0 draw on their tournament debut as the tiny African island nation reached the last 32, where they took Lionel Messi's Argentina to extra time before bowing out.
Before that game against Spain in Atlanta, Vozinha was just a journeyman goalkeeper who had spent his career shuffling between unremarkable clubs in Portugal, Cyprus and Slovakia.
A clean sheet against the World Cup favourites saw his Instagram account balloon from 50,000 followers to several million in a matter of hours. He now has 27.5 million followers.
Vozinha shed tears after that match, because of the scale of his and the team's achievement, but also sadness at not being able to obtain a visa for his mother to be there.
After joining Colo Colo, Chile's most successful side from the capital Santiago, he was unveiled at their Estadio Monumental before thousands of fans to a backdrop of fireworks.
He has been recruited by global brands like Adidas, Pepsi and Red Bull to be the face of advertising campaigns.
Vozinha also recently attended the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London as he came sixth in the voting for the the men's goalkeeper of the year prize.
However, on the field the player who spent last season in Portugal's second division has toiled.
By the start of November he had appeared in only five games out of a possible 14 for Colo Colo, who won the Copa Libertadores, South America's equivalent of the Champions League, in 1991.
He was expected to be a substitute again this weekend, as his new team closes in on the Chilean title, and a place in next year's Copa Libertadores.
"I came here with the intention of playing in the Libertadores, but my focus is on this week, which could be very important for Colo Colo. My future will be decided after that. I'm not thinking about that," Vozinha told reporters.
- Reluctant celebrity -
Vozinha's life was turned on its head following his World Cup exploits. He has moved to a new country, and went from being a virtual unknown to a celebrity with no privacy.
He worked as a rubbish collector before turning professional. To put his number of Instagram followers into perspective: the entire population of his native Cape Verde is only a little over 500,000.
"I've lost my peace and tranquillity," Vozinha told British newspaper The Observer.
"I no longer have any privacy, or at least much less than I used to. Now I go out, I go to a restaurant, and there's always someone who wants to take a photo with me or asks me for an autograph. Or, worse, someone is filming me."
In the first few weeks after signing for Colo Colo, Vozinha regularly went to a bakery in the wealthy Vitacura neighbourhood of Santiago.
"I think it was good for him to go because he felt welcomed and was able to chat to people," Gustavo Cassin, the manager of the cafe called Metissage, tells AFP.
Cassin and Vozinha avoided discussing football. The player would talk longingly about his home country as he waited for his morning croissant.
- Will he stay? -
The past, when he combined playing with teaching beach volleyball, is now a distant memory.
"To be honest, if I were offered the life I have today or the life I had before, I'd choose the one I had before," he told The Observer.
In Chile, media are speculating as to whether Vozinha will remain into 2027 -- he signed a six-month contract with Colo Colo extendable by a year only if he plays enough minutes.
He has faced criticism, with Chilean goalkeeping legend Claudio Bravo, formerly of Barcelona and Manchester City, questioning his ability.
"He has made several errors in situations that require coordination," said the ex-Chile captain. "And if you don't have coordination, you'll never do it."
Vozinha has a handful of games remaining before his contract runs out, and perhaps with it his Chilean adventure.

item.title: England's injured Tongue out of Australia white-ball tour
item.description:
England fast bowler Josh Tongue has been ruled out of their white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury and will return home for treatment, the team said Sunday.
Tongue arrived in Perth last week ahead of England's three-match ODI and five-game T20 series, but sat out their 92-run one-day warm-up win over Western Australia on Saturday.
"Josh Tongue has been ruled out of the white-ball tour of Australia due to a left big toe injury," team officials said. "Tongue will return to the UK to undergo further assessment."
Batsman Jacob Bethell, who is returning from knee surgery, also missed the game, where Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid excelled.
Pace spearhead Archer took 3-34 and spinner Rashid 4-35 as Western Australia were bowled out for 159, having been set 252 to win.
Ben Duckett cracked 59 and Liam Dawson an unbeaten 44 for England, who open the ODI leg of the tour in Perth on Friday before the series moves to Adelaide and Hobart.
It is England's first time back in Australia since being crushed 4-1 in the 2025-26 Ashes Test series.

item.title: Antonelli 'ready for anything' in Sao Paulo Grand Prix
item.description:
New world champion Kimi Antonelli said he will be "ready for anything" in Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix when he starts alongside 2025 champion Lando Norris on the front row.
Elevated one place thanks to Mercedes team-mate George Russell's five-place penalty for taking new power unit parts, the 20-year-old Italian was satisfied, but self-critical after finishing third in Saturday's rain-hit qualifying.
"I was a bit too cautious I think," he said.
"I was trying to understand this track in the wet for the first time and it has always been dry here so far in the past. But I felt good in the dry and not so good in the wet!
"I made two big mistakes and it wasn't ideal, but all in all I think that tomorrow, we have a good chance."
He added that he felt cautious about the weather ahead after the long stormy session on Saturday.
"It was very tricky. To be fair, I didn't really know what to expect. Obviously, I have never driven here in the wet, so I didn't know what was coming and I struggled a little bit on the inters.
"I made a big mistake, almost went off in Turn Five, but it still was enough for P3, so I’m happy with that.
"Let's see what the weather is – but overall, you know, I am going to be ready for anything as the weather has been very unpredictable. We will try to be ready for anything."
Russell, who qualified second, was unhappy not to take pole after being told by his Mercedes race engineer to ease off on his final flying lap.
"I felt more like myself and I could fight for pole on every lap," said the British driver.
"It's the first time I've felt that confident in the car for a while and it's in the wet so I don't understand that.
"Congrats to Lando – but that lap was definitely a pole lap! It was a misjudgement on our side and we need to understand what happened. Yes, the rain was coming down but we should have finished the lap."

item.title: World No.1 Rybakina withdraws from WTA Finals due to virus
item.description:
World number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from the WTA Finals at Indian Wells on Saturday due to a viral illness.
Defending champion Rybakina said in a statement that she was "not physically ready to compete" in the traditional season-ender, which starts Sunday, and would focus on resting and recovering for her 2027 campaign.
"I am really sad to inform all my fans and supporters that I unfortunately have to withdraw from the WTA Finals this year," Rybakina said in a statement.
"I've had an incredible season but my body is just not physically ready to compete.
"I'm going to spend some time resting and recovering at home and getting myself ready for the 2027 season."
A WTA spokesman later confirmed that the official reason for Rybakina's withdrawal "is a viral illness."
Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk will take Rybakina's place in Group One at the tournament.
Rybakina rose to the top of the world rankings for the first time in September with a victory at the US Open in New York, where she defeated Aryna Sabalenka in the final.
But last month, Rybakina withdrew from the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo with a neck injury, a day after she secured the year-end world number one ranking with a win in her opening match.
The achievement capped a year in which Rybakina also won the Australian Open in January.
She now has three Grand Slam titles, her first coming at Wimbledon in 2022.
Rybakina went undefeated at the 2025 edition of the WTA Finals in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia as the last qualifier.
This year's WTA Finals were originally scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia, but in July were moved to Indian Wells, California.
The decision was taken following US military strikes on Iran in February and the subsequent war in the region.
Several more sports events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country.
"The WTA Finals is a very special tournament and I wish everyone the best of luck this week. Can't wait to be back in Indian Wells in March," said Rybakina in a statement released.

item.title: Defiant Khawaja defends re-igniting ball-tampering scandal
item.description:
Usman Khawaja insisted Sunday he did not "throw anyone under the bus" by claiming the entire Australian team was in on the 2018 "Sandpapergate" plot and defended taking eight years to go public.
The retired batsman re-ignited the infamous ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town on Saturday ahead of the release of his autobiography this week, where a chapter is dedicated to the issue.
He alleged that it was not just Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft -- who were all subsequently banned -- who were responsible.
"It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," he said.
Khawaja claimed Australia also employed the tactic during the previous Test at Port Elizabeth.
In response Darren Lehmann, who was head coach at the time, denied there was widespread knowledge of the plot while Cricket Australia said it was "comfortable" with the findings of its original investigation.
That probe found only Smith, Warner and Bancroft were in the know.
"When I mentioned it was all of us, that's implying that whether we like it or not, we're all responsible for what happened together as a team," Khawaja said in a lengthy Instagram post on Sunday.
"We need to take that collectively. That is all."
He added: "I haven't thrown anyone under the bus.
"The guys that are currently in the team right now and the other people that were there on the South African tour, including me, we're not the victims.
"These three guys (Smith, Warner and Bancroft) took the blame for all of us.
"They're the victims ... people telling them that they're cheats, getting nailed by the crowd. Public humiliation."
Khawaja, who retired this year after 88 Tests, defended waiting so long to make the claims, denying it was a marketing ploy to sell his book.
He said he wanted to go public in 2018 once Smith, Warner and Bancroft were suspended.
"But Smudge (Smith) being the man and leader he was, he talked me out of it.
"He wanted to take the blame. I argued with him, but he was having none of it. That's the first time I tried to come out."
Khawaja said he again almost spoke up in 2021 when bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly that they knew about the ball-tampering.
But after extensive talks with then-coach Justin Langer he decided not to.
The 39-year-old said he never felt comfortable talking after that while back in the Australian team from 2022.
"Call me a chicken or whatever you want. I didn't know how to do it because I was still in the team," Khawaja said. "I was always conscious of putting my team first, but I'm not in that team anymore."

item.title: How to host a diwali party at home in two hours
item.description:
Diwali celebrations do not always require elaborate preparations. With a little planning and a carefully selected menu, hosts can arrange a home party for friends and family in just two hours.
Welcome guests with two simple beverage options. Mix store-bought soft drinks with crushed mint leaves, lemon juice, jaljeera and a pinch of mineral salt to prepare a mojito-style mocktail. Lassi or lemonade can be served as an alternative.
There is no need to prepare several varieties of drinks. Serving two options in attractive glasses is enough to make the refreshments appealing.
Papri chaat is a quick option for an appetizer. Arrange papri on a plate and top it with aloo kabli, made with chickpeas or peas. Add coriander leaves, tamarind chutney and crispy fried noodles for extra flavour.
Ready-made aloo kabli from a local shop can also be used to save preparation time.
Store-bought French fries, cheese balls and chicken nuggets can be prepared quickly in an air fryer or frying pan.
For a homemade option, cut boneless chicken into small pieces and marinate with ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, black pepper, egg and cornflour. Fry the pieces shortly before guests arrive to make chicken pakora.
Serve the snacks with a dip made from mayonnaise and tomato ketchup. A simple salad of sliced onions and cucumbers, seasoned with lemon juice, salt and chaat masala, can complement the fried items.
For lighter options, include nuts, roasted makhana or boiled eggs fried with butter, onions and green chillies.
There is no need for an elaborate main-course spread. Biryani or morog polao can be served with a meat dish. Alternatively, rumali roti or naan can accompany a chicken or mutton preparation.
For a homemade menu, sweet fried rice with cashews and raisins can be paired with chicken or mutton. Vegetarian alternatives include chhana kofta and navratan korma.
When time is limited, focus on presentation rather than increasing the number of dishes. Arrange sauces and dips in small bowls alongside the snacks, and use separate glasses for drinks and an attractive plate for the salad.
Setting the table before guests arrive can also reduce last-minute pressure. With a few simple preparations, a welcoming Diwali gathering can be arranged within two hours.

item.title: Samira Khan Mahi to represent Bangladesh at Miss Universe 2026
item.description:

According to the organisers, Mahi will represent Bangladesh at the 75th Miss Universe competition in Puerto Rico, with activities scheduled to begin on November 11.
Speaking after her win, Mahi said her parents had encouraged her to “go and conquer the world” and asked for the public’s prayers as she prepares for the international competition.

item.title: Body of municipal Jubo Dal leader recovered in Bandarban
item.description:

The deceased, 38-year-old Sharif, was the joint convener of the Municipal Jubo Dal's Ward 9 unit and worked as a mason. He was the son of Zahir and a resident of Talukdarpara in the town.
His bloodied body was found in a stream in the Kasaipara area of the district town.
According to police and local residents, people heading to work on Sunday morning spotted a man lying in the stream with blood on his body. His nose and mouth were bleeding. They informed the police, who arrived at the scene, recovered the body and took it to Bandarban Sadar Hospital.
Locals suspect that Sharif may have slipped and fallen into the stream while descending towards it, resulting in his death.
Bandarban Superintendent of Police Md Wahabul Islam Khandaker said police had recovered the body from the stream. The exact cause of death would be determined after an autopsy.

The equation was not particularly complicated. Bangladesh would qualify for the semi-finals if Sri Lanka beat or drew with Bhutan. Today, that off-field calculation was settled on the pitch as well.

The match between Bhutan and Sri Lanka at the National Stadium ended in a 2–2 draw, securing Bangladesh a place in the semi-finals of the SAFF Championship for the seventh time.

The result also kept Bhutan’s hopes alive. However, to reach the last four, Bhutan will now have to depend on the outcome of the Bangladesh–Sri Lanka match.

A single point for Sri Lanka in that game will be enough to secure its semi-final spot. Bangladesh, meanwhile, must win by a margin of at least two goals to knock Sri Lanka out.

For Bangladesh coach Thomas Dooley, today was an opportunity to watch their opponents up close. The team could have trained in the afternoon, but Dooley had a different plan.

After finishing their training session at 10:00 am, he took the players to the National Stadium. He wanted to watch both matches of the day from the stands, particularly to assess Sri Lanka’s style of play, strengths and weaknesses.

Bangladesh are scheduled to face Sri Lanka on 11 November.

Along with the chance to study their opponents, Dooley also got an entertaining match to watch. Two goals came within a span of two minutes.

The excitement began in the 34th minute when Bhutan took the lead through Dawa Tshering. But just a minute later, Oliver Kelaart brought Sri Lanka level with a stunning strike.

His shot from outside the box was a beauty. Sri Lanka attacked again in the 43rd minute, and Wasim Razeek put them 2–1 ahead with a precise header from Kelaart’s cross.

Across 46 matches in the previous 13 editions of the SAFF Championship, Bangladesh have conceded 52 goals. Of those, 18 came after the 70th minute.

Bhutan tried to fight their way back into the game after the break and were awarded a penalty in the 68th minute. But Sri Lanka goalkeeper Sujan Perera saved captain Chencho’s spot kick. Chencho did not have to rue the missed penalty for long, however.

He scored a brilliant goal in the 76th minute to bring Bhutan level. The score remained 2–2, opening the door for Bangladesh to reach the semifinals.

Meanwhile, Bangladesh’s preparations are also progressing, with coach Dooley feeling more at ease than before. Sheikh Morsalin took part in the entire training session today. However, Tapu Barman has yet to fully recover from his injury. Instead of training with the team, the defender did some running separately under the supervision of the physiotherapist.

Dooley placed particular emphasis on defensive work during today’s training session. One of Bangladesh’s longstanding problems has been conceding goals late in matches, and the statistics underline that concern.

Across 46 matches in the previous 13 editions of the SAFF Championship, Bangladesh have conceded 52 goals. Of those, 18 came after the 70th minute.

Maintaining defensive concentration until the final whistle therefore remains a major challenge for Bangladesh. Alongside sharpening the attack, the coach is urging his players to protect their goal right until the end.

In the first match of the day, Pakistan had already secured their semi-final place with a 3–0 victory over the Maldives. With the day’s two matches concluded, Bangladesh and Pakistan have now secured their places in the last four.

However, attendance at the stadium was disappointing. Even after offering a 50 per cent discount on tickets for both matches, the organisers failed to fill the stands.

item.title: Inside Tongi’s drug empire, where gangs defy repeated crackdowns
item.description:
Barely 20 metres from a mosque and 50 metres from a ferry crossing in Tongi, hundreds of people gather in broad daylight to buy, sell and consume narcotics.
Makeshift drug dens operate openly, surveillance cameras monitor visitors, and armed groups allegedly control access to parts of the neighbourhood.
This is Haji Mazar Basti, a sprawling settlement on the banks of the Turag River in Gazipur, where repeated police raids, eviction drives and the destruction of drug dens have failed to dismantle an entrenched narcotics network.
An infographic highlights conditions in Haji Mazar Basti, outlining its dense population, open drug trade, makeshift shelters, surveillance measures and challenges in law enforcement.
The extent of the alleged criminal control is such that even police officers acknowledge the dangers of entering the area.
“Even we, the police, are afraid to go there. It’s as if it’s a separate state within Bangladesh,” a police official told Dhaka Tribune on condition of anonymity.
The officer said law enforcement personnel had previously encountered violent resistance while gathering intelligence and conducting operations.
“Even when we go in a group, we are unable to accomplish anything. I once went there with a colleague to gather intelligence and barely managed to make it back out.”
A Dhaka Tribune investigation on November 6 found narcotics being sold and consumed openly across the settlement, while residents alleged that the criminal network continued to operate under the influence of politically connected individuals.
The investigation itself turned violent when three Dhaka Tribune journalists were attacked by suspected drug traders, taken to a secluded location and beaten by a group of around 20 to 25 people.
Spread across approximately five acres near Abdullahpur, Haji Mazar Basti is home to an estimated 30,000 people.
The settlement is accessible through two roads from Tongi and from the Turag River.
At its centre stands the shrine and mosque of Hazrat Syed Shah Bogdadi (RA), surrounded by densely packed tin-roofed houses and multistorey structures.
Residents alleged that the narcotics business was previously controlled by individuals affiliated with the Awami League but that influence shifted towards local BNP leaders and members of its affiliated organisations following the political change on August 5, 2024.
During the visit, at least five offices bearing the signboards of the BNP and its affiliated organisations were observed at different entrances to the settlement.
Most were closed, while two were open but unattended.
Residents claimed that many of these offices previously displayed Awami League signboards, which were replaced following the July uprising.
Billboards featuring local BNP leaders and prospective ward councillor candidates were also visible.
However, the presence of political offices and billboards does not independently establish that their occupants control or benefit from the drug trade. The allegations of political patronage remain unverified.
During the investigation, reporters witnessed suspected narcotics transactions and drug consumption at several locations.
Residents said cannabis, yaba, phensedyl, pethidine, charas, opium and locally produced and foreign liquor were readily available.
They also alleged that illegal firearms were traded in the area.
At Jhilik Tea Store, a grocery and tea shop in a narrow alley, five young men were observed consuming what appeared to be yaba and cannabis.
When the journalists approached, eight women standing outside the shop ushered the men indoors and asked the reporters to leave.
Residents alleged that several influential women, commonly addressed as “bhabis” by buyers and sellers, played important roles in the narcotics network.
Their identities and specific involvement could not be independently established.
The most striking scenes emerged near the Ijtema ground, where dozens of makeshift shelters had been erected behind toilet buildings numbered 26 and 27.
At least 30 to 40 shelters made of cloth were visible, reportedly rented out to drug users at different rates.
Around noon, approximately 200 people were gathered in front of and behind the buildings, with suspected drug sales and consumption taking place openly.
Some individuals invited the journalists to consume narcotics, while members of a local youth group instructed visitors to remove their masks before entering certain shelters.
A mosque stood approximately 20 metres away, while a ferry crossing was about 50 metres from the site.
A government office belonging to the Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments was also located within the settlement, where drug activity was reported nearby.
The suspected narcotics network appeared to operate its own surveillance arrangements.
CCTV cameras monitored entrances, while unfamiliar visitors were reportedly questioned and required to obtain permission by telephone before entering certain sections.
Residents said newcomers sometimes had their belongings inspected.
Tongi West Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Arifur Rahman acknowledged that police had previously attempted to dismantle the surveillance network.
“We recently conducted an operation in the area, destroyed all the CCTV cameras installed by them, demolished their drug dens and disconnected electricity connections,” he said.
However, surveillance arrangements were reportedly restored after the operation.
The apparent ability to rebuild such infrastructure raises questions about the lasting effectiveness of enforcement measures.
Police and other authorities have conducted several operations in Haji Mazar Basti, but suspected drug trading has repeatedly resurfaced.
On July 22, police disconnected electricity and internet connections to rooms belonging to around 300 identified suspected drug traders.
Following the operation, Gazipur Metropolitan Police Additional Commissioner Mohammad Belayet Hossain described the scale of open drug consumption in the settlement as an exceptional and longstanding concern.
In August, Rajuk demolished around 100 illegal structures and suspected drug dens on approximately three bighas of land.
Another eviction drive was conducted on August 31 near the Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments office.
Police raids between May and subsequent months reportedly uncovered more than 100 rooms and hidden tunnels allegedly used for drug trading and escape.
Some facilities reportedly contained air-conditioned rooms where influential individuals allegedly gathered to consume narcotics.
Yet residents say the operations have failed to permanently dismantle the network.
The concerns extend beyond Haji Mazar Basti.
Residents identified several other locations in Tongi where narcotics were allegedly sold, including Bank Math Basti, Keranir Tek, Amtali Basti, Millgate Basti, Ershadnagar, Shilmun, Morkun, Arichpur, Gazipura, Khortail Madina Para, Pagaar and Gopalpur.
They alleged that disputes over narcotics distribution and mugging had triggered violent confrontations and killings.
On September 28, Rafiqul Islam Joy was killed in Bank Math Basti, while Nurul Islam was allegedly killed in Gopalpur on September 1 following a dispute involving yaba, according to local sources.
The settlement has also attracted scrutiny following the death of former Air Force officer KM Tahsif Sauri, whose body was recovered from the Turag River after he reportedly visited the area.
The circumstances of his death and any connection to the alleged narcotics network have not been established.
Gazipur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Md Ashiq Sayeed, who newly appointed and joined the office on Sunday, told Dhaka Tribune that the police would adopt a zero-tolerance policy against drugs.
“I have joined Gazipur Metropolitan Police today. We will maintain a zero-tolerance policy towards drugs. We will take all necessary measures, including arresting drug dealers and criminals and conducting operations to eliminate crime, to make the entire Gazipur, including Tongi Mazar Basti, free from drugs and terrorism.
“Our specialised police units are fully prepared to carry out such operations, and we will take all necessary steps. We will also launch a strong crackdown on drug dealers in Tongi Mazar Basti very soon,” he said.
OC Arifur Rahman said suspected drug traders had adapted their operations following earlier eviction drives, establishing mobile distribution points around the Turag River and Ijtema ground.
He said suspects frequently escaped towards areas under Dhaka Metropolitan Police jurisdiction or dispersed through the Ijtema grounds when police attempted raids.
Discussions had taken place with senior officers about conducting larger operations, he added.
For residents of Haji Mazar Basti, however, the repeated return of suspected drug traders after enforcement operations remains a pressing concern.

item.title: DT journalists held hostage, tortured at gunpoint by Tongi drug gang
item.description:
Three Dhaka Tribune journalists investigating alleged drug trafficking in Gazipur’s Tongi were held captive for nearly three hours, brutally assaulted and threatened with death at gunpoint on Friday, in an attack that has exposed the apparent grip of criminal gangs over an area where another journalist was reportedly abducted and tortured less than two weeks earlier.
The attackers forced the journalists to consume a sedative, staged photographs and videos intended for blackmail, and seized their cameras, phones, money and identification documents before releasing them with a warning never to report on criminal activities in the area again.
The incident occurred at Hazir Mazar slum under Tongi West Police Station, where the journalists had gone to investigate drug trafficking and other crimes.
The victims were Dhaka Tribune reporters Rabiul Hasan and Asiful Islam Rifat, and photojournalist Abir Ahmed Supto.
According to a written complaint filed by Rabiul at Tongi West Police Station on Friday evening, a group of 20 to 25 armed individuals attacked the journalists while they were gathering information in the area.
The assailants allegedly held a pistol to their heads, threatened to mutilate them with sharp weapons and forcibly took them to a nearby location.
There, they were beaten repeatedly and held captive for approximately three hours.
At one stage, the attackers forced them to drink a liquid containing a sedative before placing narcotics and cash in front of them and compelling them to record false confessions.
The journalists believe the recordings were intended to blackmail them and prevent further reporting on drug-related crimes.
Describing the ordeal, Rabiul said the team had spent around an hour and a half collecting evidence of drug trafficking before being confronted.
“My phone contained clear photos and videos, including distinct images of drug dealers and footage of their various distribution hubs,” he said.
He alleged that the attackers had monitored their movements through CCTV cameras and demanded access to his phone.
“When I refused, they assaulted me, seized the phone at gunpoint and deleted everything.”
Rabiul said the attackers repeatedly struck the journalists with a firearm and threatened to shoot them.
“Upon discovering the data we had collected for our report, they held us captive until evening, planning to kill us. They repeatedly struck us with a revolver and even attempted to open fire,” he said.
He claimed that around 200 people were openly buying and selling narcotics in the vicinity while the journalists were being held.
The location, he said, was approximately 20 metres from a mosque and 50 metres from a ferry crossing.
“Yet, throughout this long period, no member of any law enforcement agency arrived at the scene,” he said.
The journalists were eventually released after an unidentified individual contacted them through a video call and demanded that they stop reporting on drug trafficking and criminal activities in the area.
Fearing for their lives, they agreed.
The attackers allegedly issued further death threats before allowing them to leave.
The injured journalists received initial treatment at Shaheed Ahsan Ullah Master General Hospital in Tongi before being referred for advanced medical care.
The attack follows a similar incident involving Mohin Uddin Ripon, Gazipur district correspondent for the daily Kalbela, who was abducted at gunpoint in the same area on October 26.
According to allegations surrounding that incident, Ripon was beaten, tortured and held for a ransom of Tk1 crore.
His abductors stripped him and recorded compromising footage involving a woman, apparently as a means of intimidation and blackmail.
During Friday’s attack, the Dhaka Tribune journalists said their captors showed them photographs and videos of Ripon’s ordeal.
The apparent repetition of the same tactics has raised serious concerns among local journalists about the risks of reporting on organised crime in Tongi.
The recent recovery of a retired Air Force officer’s body from the Turag River, followed by the discovery of his motorcycle in the Mazar Basti area, has further heightened concerns about criminal activity in the locality.
No connection between that death and the attacks on journalists has been established.
A police official, speaking on condition of anonymity, acknowledged the difficulties law enforcement personnel face in operating in the area.
“Even we, the police, are afraid to go there. It’s as if it’s a separate state within Bangladesh,” the official said.
“Even when we go in a group, we are unable to accomplish anything. I once went there with a colleague to gather intelligence and barely managed to make it back out.”
The official described the situation as extremely dangerous and suggested journalists should avoid entering the slum to investigate criminal activities.
Gazipur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Israil Howlader, whose final day in the position was Saturday, told Dhaka Tribune that action would be taken against those responsible for the attack.
He said operations would soon be launched in and around Tongi Mazar Basti to identify and arrest suspected drug dealers and criminals.
The newly appointed GMP commissioner Md Ashiq Sayeed said he had only recently assumed office and was still gathering details about the incident.
“I have just taken charge and learned about the incident. We will investigate the matter and take appropriate action,” he said.
Tongi West Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Arifur Rahman confirmed that an officer had been assigned to investigate the written complaint.
He said legal action would follow the preliminary investigation. “Six drug users and two drug dealers had been arrested from the area over the past two days," he added.
According to the OC, drug dealers shifted their operations following an earlier eviction drive at Mazar Basti, establishing mobile distribution networks around the Turag River and Ijtema grounds.
He said suspects frequently escaped towards areas under Dhaka Metropolitan Police jurisdiction or dispersed through the Ijtema grounds when police attempted raids.
Discussions had already taken place with senior officials about conducting larger operations, he added.

item.title: Holding the world accountable for the climate crisis
item.description:
As world leaders assemble in Antalya, Türkiye, for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), it is safe to say that the threat of climate change has long ceased to be an abstract projection and has become the most significant existential catastrophe for the entire planet.
This is particularly true for a nation such as ours. With global heat records continuously shattered and fragile coastal ecosystems buckling under systemic salinization and relentless riverine erosion, Bangladesh remains among the most affected nations - due to a crisis it had virtually no part in creating.
For decades, global climate summits have yielded ambitious rhetoric, bureaucratic inertia, and pledges devoid of enforcement. At COP31, our diplomatic delegation, and indeed others from the Global South, must enter negotiations not to petition for international goodwill, but to demand the immediate, enforceable execution of climate justice.
The bedrock of our negotiating must reflect the economic reality we face as a result of climate change. Bangladeshi leadership must resolutely hold the world’s primary industrial polluters, ie the Global North accountable.
At a time when Bangladesh is experiencing among its most challenging economic issues, the effects of climate change continue to destroy infrastructure, deplete agricultural yields, and cause mass human displacement. Yet, it has been sad to see international countermeasures remain egregiously disproportionate.
The global Loss and Damage Fund, which was secured after years of arduous diplomacy, remains severely undercapitalized, with current allocation frameworks failing to address the true scope of vulnerability.
At COP31, Bangladesh must lead the coalition of climate-vulnerable states in advocating for legally binding financial commitments and doing away with the unreliable paradigm of voluntary contributions that major economies routinely disregard.
Beyond loss and damage, we must also prioritize direct, grant-based adaptation capital. Bangladesh cannot continue to accept climate finance structured as debt-bearing loans, which serve only to exacerbate existing foreign reserve strains.
Global climate equity is not optional, and COP31 must mark a turning point where Bangladesh plays its part in compelling the international community to honour its obligations.

item.title: Borrowing for our future
item.description:
The World Bank’s support to improve the quality of primary education and address learning gaps among children in Bangladesh is certainly positive news.
Aimed at improving learning outcomes, upgrading classrooms, providing essential learning materials, and strengthening school management for over 26 million children from pre-primary to Grade 5, we must be thankful that steps are being taken to improve the quality of a system where World Bank data show that around 50% of 10-year-old children in the country cannot read and understand a simple text appropriate for their age and grade level.
With that said, the approval of the $300 million financing package, while undeniably being a critical injection of resources into our foundational schooling system, must be recognized for what it is.
Every time international loans are secured for public development, a familiar shadow looms over the country: The deep-seated fear of administrative waste, corruption, bureaucratic leakage, and poor execution.
For decades, foreign-funded projects, regardless of the sector they are in, have too often been characterized by inflated costs and delayed rollouts that fail to bring about meaningful transformation.
Pouring hundreds of millions of dollars without ironclad execution safeguards is an unacceptable gamble. As such, the authorities concerned must recognize that this funding carries a heavy moral and economic obligation.
Every single taka must be channeled directly into measurable pedagogical improvements. There is no room for procurement corruption or administrative foot-dragging.
Foreign loans must build the nation’s future, not line the pockets of the influential and powerful, or disappear into bureaucratic black holes. If we are going to borrow to educate our children, we must ensure the investment delivers a measurable return -- transforming public primary education from a broken system into one that adds to our prosperity.

item.title: Journalists across Asia face police action in growing crackdown on movements
item.description:
“I was put in a bus. I showed them that I have an ID card and a mic ID, and asked them why I was being detained. But they didn’t want us to show how protesters were being manhandled,” said 28-year-old Pragya Mishra, who runs a news outlet called Ulta Chasma uc.
On October 11, 2026, Mishra was covering the protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at RK Ashram in Delhi. While reporting, Mishra says her cameraperson Anuj Kumar (23) was pulled by his hair by police personnel. When she went to protect him and inform the police that they were from the media, she was also forcibly put inside a bus with a few other journalists.
She told Asian Dispatch that she was being taken to a detention centre in Rajendra Nagar. The bus, however, was intercepted and stopped by other journalists. She says that the police eventually dropped them at Connaught Place.
Mishra was not the only journalist who faced police action during the recent protests held across the country against Kumar over the alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls.
The protest against CEC Kumar is linked to the alleged irregularities in the ongoing SIR process, which has reportedly resulted in the deletion of around 13 crore names from electoral rolls.
It gained momentum after a report published by The Indian Express dated September 24 found that Election Commissioners Sukhir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over a 10-month period.
According to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), at least 43 instances of journalists being detained were recorded. Journalists from several news organizations such as The Wire, Scroll, The Quint, Newslaundry, as well as freelance journalists were detained -- some were even heckled, assaulted, and forced to delete what they had documented on the ground.
The Press Club of India, along with other journalists’ associations, condemned the detentions and said that the police took the step even after journalists displayed their press cards.
It further mentioned that the police seized the phones and reporting equipment of some of the journalists. The statement referred to the developments as a “blatant attack on the freedom of the press.”
Commenting on the situation, Reporters Without Borders (RSF) told us: “What we are witnessing is not simply excessive policing during demonstrations, it is part of a broader pattern of restrictions that undermines the ability of journalists to report freely on matters of public interest, particularly when their reporting exposes the conduct of the authorities.”
RSF is an international non-profit working towards protecting the rights of journalists/press. According to their 2026 World Press Freedom Index , India ranks 157 out of 180 countries in press freedom. The body also highlighted that press freedom remains a major concern across Asia, where the media faces restrictions in covering politically sensitive events and protests.
CPJ’s annual report on jailed journalists, released in January 2026, noted that 330 journalists were behind the bars globally as of December 1, 2025. Of these, one-third were in Asia -- China and Myanmar were found to be the leading jailers in the region.
It’s important to note that this number from Asia excludes jailed journalists from Central and West Asia (referred to as the Middle East in the graph). Those are marked separately in CPJ’s database.
Speaking to Asian Dispatch , Kunal Majumder, Asia-Pacific program coordinator, Committee to Project Journalists (CPJ), said that journalism is under attack across the region and added: “In South Asia, the focus is largely on over-regulation of the online space; apart from SLAPP [Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation] suits, physical violence remains a grave problem.”
Expressing concern about the situation in India, Majumder said that India has a responsibility to uphold press freedom and “serve as a role model for other countries in the Global South.”
This pattern where journalists have faced action, have been assaulted, detained or arrested by law enforcement agencies is consistent across other Asian countries.
For instance: the situation for journalists in Bangladesh during the 2024 July uprising was alarming. The International Federation of Journalists (IFJ) estimated that at least 160 journalists were reportedly injured while covering the nationwide protests as of July 31, 2024.
RSF noted that five journalists were allegedly killed by police bullets between July 15, 2024 and August 5, 2024, and one was killed during clashes between two factions.
CPJ, in a report published on July 26, 2024, detailed the reports of police attacks on journalists. It said that on July 16, 2024, police personnel fired metal pellets at journalists Mehedi Mamun, Abdur Rahman Khan Sarjil, Wajahatul Islam, and Jubayer Ahmed. This happened despite them identifying themselves as journalists.
The next day, July 17, 2024, Abdullah Al Mamum, a correspondent with Prothom Alo, was reportedly beaten with rifles and batons by police personnel while he was recording the police action against students. Mamum told CPJ that he showed them his press card but he was beaten and the police fired a rubber bullet at him while he was trying to flee.
More recently, Ernest Cruz, a reporter working with Bulatlat in the Philippines, was assaulted by the Quezon City Police on October 19, 2026, while he was covering a protest led by farmer groups. According to RSF, Cruz was assaulted despite identifying himself as a journalist.
A similar incident happened on September 21, 2025, when eight journalists covering the anti-government protests in Manila were harassed, assaulted, and obstructed. They alleged that police used shields to deliberately obstruct media coverage. The usage of tear gas and water cannons near to where journalists were also posed direct harm to their safety.
At least nine journalists in Sri Lanka were injured during the anti-government protests in 2022. A freelance journalist, Sumedha Sanjeewa Gallage, was reportedly attacked by the police while he was covering a demonstration outside the president’s residence. As per reports , he lost partial vision in his right eye following the attack.
The 2026 CPJ analysis also found that the greatest incidence of torture and beatings of journalists has occurred in Iran since 1992. Between 2022 and 2025, 71 journalists were imprisoned in Iran.
